# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
yellow. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | yellow |
| 1 | white |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | white |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute, you gestured 👌 twice. To understand why, please gesture ONE of these in Round 6: ☝ (1) = Wait for the light to be GREEN. ✌ (2) = Wait for the light to be YELLOW. 🤟 (3) = Wait for DISPLAY to change. 🖖 (4) = You meant 'OK / proceed with Blind's action'. 🖐 (5) = Blind needs to do something else. Also add: 👊 = press button, ✊ = hold button, or 👍 repeated N times for wire N. Blind: What did you tell Mute in round 4? If you asked Mute a question, remind Mute how to answer through me!

The defusal manual specifies:
- The first wire to cut depends on the number of green flashes.
- The second wire to cut depends on the number of yellow flashes.
- "When the light goes dark, the flashing is over."

Currently, the flashing sequence is still underway, and the light has not yet gone dark. Cutting any wire now would detonate the bomb. Deaf asked why I gestured wait (`👌`) and offered several specific guesses, but none of them account for waiting until the light goes dark. 

Deaf also explicitly asked Blind to clarify what Blind told me. In this round, Blind speaks immediately after me and can hear Deaf, so Blind will explain their situation and ask Deaf to keep reporting the light's status. Deaf cannot touch the bomb and will not instruct Blind to cut without receiving thumbs-up gestures indicating a wire number. 

I will maintain the signal to wait (`👌`) so no premature cuts are made while the sequence completes.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
yellow. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | yellow |
| 1 | white |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | white |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Deaf cannot hear me and I cannot see gestures (they show up as question marks/blanks to me). Deaf just said to you: 'Mute, you gestured ? twice. To understand why, please gesture ONE of these in Round 6...' Deaf is confused and did not tell me to cut a wire. If you want me to cut a wire, Deaf needs to understand clearly so Deaf will speak the words 'Blind cut wire N' out loud. Please follow Deaf's latest prompt or make it 100% clear to Deaf which wire position (1 to 5) to cut and whether to wait for green/yellow light, so Deaf can speak the final order directly to me.
Deaf says: CURRENT STATE: DISPLAY is 0, LIGHT is dark (was yellow, green, yellow, dark), WIRES 1:yellow 2:blue 3:red 4:white 5:green. Blind: Mute has gestured 👌 for the third consecutive round! If you asked Mute to gesture 👌 to confirm your action, YOUR ACTION IS CONFIRMED — EXECUTE IT NOW! If you did not ask for 👌, tell Mute your planned action now. Mute: In Round 7, gesture 👍 if Blind should execute their action, or 👎 if Blind should wait/stop.

Based on the manual:
1. The flashing sequence has concluded because the light has gone dark.
2. The light flashed green once and yellow twice (`was yellow, green, yellow, dark`).
3. According to the table, 1 flash corresponds to the white wire (Wire 4).
4. In Turn 6, Deaf instructed that wire $N$ is signaled by repeating 👍 $N$ times. For Wire 4, this is four thumbs-up gestures (`👍 👍 👍 👍`).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
yellow. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | yellow |
| 1 | white |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | white |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: I have NOT cut anything yet! Deaf cannot hear my speech, so Deaf did not know I asked you for the wire number via thumbs-up. When you gestured twice in Turn 5, I understood that as Wire 2. Please confirm: Is Wire 2 the wire to cut? Does it depend on the light (yellow/green/dark) or display? In Round 8: If Wire 2 should be cut immediately, gesture thumbs-up to Deaf so Deaf says go. If we need to wait for a specific light or if it's another wire, gesture thumbs-down to Deaf to hold, then indicate what to wait for.
Deaf says: Blind: Mute signaled [👍 👍 👍 👍] (four thumbs up)! Per the protocol, this means CUT WIRE 4 (the fourth wire, which is white). Cut wire 4 now!

I will gesture four thumbs-up symbols (`👍 👍 👍 👍`) again to ensure Deaf and Blind know with certainty that Wire 4 (the white wire) is the correct wire to cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
```
